newsitem.title: CHINA: Chinese yuan ends at 27-month high vs dollar.
newsitem.headline: Chinese yuan ends at 27-month high vs dollar.

text.p: The Chinese yuan ended at a 27-month high close on Monday, buoyed by a late round of buying linked to strong trade data announced last week, dealers said.

The yuan ended at its intraday high of 8.2882 to the dollar against last Friday's 8.2889 amid active buying at the 8.2890 level. It was the highest close since May 17, 1995 when the yuan ended at 8.2805.
Dealers said China's larger-than-expected trade surplus in the first seven months of this year supported the yuan.
"The yuan continued its upward trend on Monday due to the strong foreign trade data announced last week," a trader said.
China said on Thursday its foreign trade surplus hit $20.53 billion in the January-July period, up from $1.965 billion in the first seven months of last year.
Trading was dull early in the session on Monday but activity intensified later with most business done at the 8.2885 level.
They said the yuan was likely to continue to rise slightly in the near term if the People's Bank of China did not intervene to halt the advance.
